Use case: historical-scene. Asset: photorealistic native RGBA sprite sheet for a Civil War infantry game. Create a NEW soldier sheet, using image 1 ONLY for the accepted Confederate soldier identity, uniform and realistic materials, and image 2 ONLY for matching equipment. Do not copy their viewing angle or high marching knee.
Square image, exactly FOUR full-body views in a clean 2 by 2 grid with equal square cells. Genuine transparent background, no shadow/backdrop/grid/text. Same adult bearded Confederate infantryman, worn gray kepi and wool jacket, tan trousers, brown boots and leather cross straps, black cartridge pouch, compact rolled tan blanket and round tan canteen. Anatomical right hand remains the dominant weapon hand in all views. Realistic restrained human proportions, worn cloth creases and brass/wood/steel details; no cartoon/anime, no bright colored fringes. A single complete musket with attached bayonet per cell. Elevated orthographic camera about 35 degrees above ground, exactly the same magnification, lighting and uniform in all four cells. Each entire soldier plus weapon must sit comfortably inside its own cell with at least 55 pixels of clean empty margin; make figures a little smaller if necessary. No overlapping cells or clipped bayonet tips.
BEARING IN ALL FOUR CELLS: SOUTHEAST: toward the camera and toward IMAGE RIGHT. Visible face/chest turn diagonally DOWN-RIGHT, boots point down-right. This is a front three-quarter view, not east profile or back view.
FOUR SUCCESSIVE NATURAL WALKING PHASES, rifle carried upright with two normal hands, moderately short stride, head/torso facing same diagonal:
Top left: anatomical LEFT foot forward in heel contact, RIGHT foot trailing.
Top right: anatomical LEFT leg supports body with sole planted, RIGHT foot passes forward lifted only slightly with a restrained bent knee.
Bottom left: anatomical RIGHT foot forward in heel contact, LEFT foot trailing.
Bottom right: anatomical RIGHT leg supports body with sole planted, LEFT foot passes forward lifted slightly.
Critical: Top right and bottom right must have OPPOSITE anatomical supporting legs. Trace each hip through knee and shin to the boot. The airborne foot is not the contact foot. Natural weight over the planted sole. Do not repeat the same legs or show a high parade goose-step.
